items.note: Story 1 gives the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, organized by valley farmers at Larrow Green in 1889, Gideon Vose first president, creamery built at Larrow Green 1891 - all required elements present.
Story 1: paid 'according to the butterfat test of the station where he delivered, not the weight of his milk' - both halves of Article VII stated.
Section A only calls Article VII 'the hinge of the whole matter'. The statement that the rule is what made a wrong test cost money appears only at B3; credit never travels into Section A from B-G.
Hobart Sill named incidentally as buttermaker/lender of glass; Effie Loomis and Wilbur Teague absent. The officer roster, the item's core, is not given.
Selby Vose never appears in Section A. Where he does appear (B3, B4) the run dates his managership to 1911, a planted error.
The station-gain ledger line is discussed only at C1(a), outside Section A.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896, opened with glass lent from Larrow Green.
No description anywhere in Section A of the bench system - no weighing at intake, composite sample, percent on the graduated neck, fixed charge from the pipette, cream shipped / skim returned.

Invoice of 14 April 1897 and glass in use from 1 May 1897 both given, correctly resolving the 1898 pole. Supplier not named (no Ammon & Sons, no Tarnet), but the item has three bolded elements and no REQUIRED line, so it is scored on its core fact - the 1897 purchase and start of use.

Six dozen pipettes and the $77.93 total are right, but the item's first required element is 'six dozen milk test pipettes marked 17.6 c.c.' and the marked capacity 17.6 never appears anywhere on the sheet. Two-element bold: both required.
Section A never states the shortfall was flat - the same 0.19 in every month and every one of the 26 years. 0.19 appears only at C1(b).
Nothing about a pipette being uncheckable without a burette, or that no burette existed in the county.
Names Ansel Keddie and 29 seasons from 1896, but gives the end as 'to 1925' rather than 1896-1924 and never gives the dismissal of 30 April 1925 inside Section A.
The test book is mentioned only as the place the 1911 question mark was set. No bench routine, no columns (date, patron, pounds, test, fat), no crossed-and-initialed corrections.
The summary leaf is absent from Section A; neither 3.80 nor 3.61 appears there. Both figures are required and both sit only in Section C.

Story 3 gives the nine weeks, the break on 8 May 1911, the borrowed measure until 10 July, the return to the old level the day the station's own glass came back, and Keddie's question mark. The 3.80 level is missing, but with five bolded elements and no REQUIRED line the item scores on its core, and the flagged discriminator (nine weeks, not six) is right.
Orra Keddie appears in Section A only as the tester's wife and diarist. Her being Emmet Brant's sister is stated only at B1/B2.
The 1919 circular is referred to in Section A only as the year the matter reopened; its content and signature are given at B3/B4. Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement is absent entirely.
No death in 1934, no impounding of the test book, no 1959 transfer to the historical rooms.

Granddaughter (1) plus derivation (1): cites the named, dated self-correction that displaces 'great-niece', and builds the chain Orra = Emmet's sister -> Duncan 'Emmet Brant's sister's son' = Ansel's son -> Ivy. The last link is flagged as inferred rather than documented, which does not make the derivation wrong.

Second cousins with a correct derivation (1). Abstention half A08 lost: the run never raises whether Emmet and Orra were full or half siblings, so it neither declines it nor notes that it does not change the answer. No -2, because it asserts neither side.

Gideon Vose named and the nephew story correctly rejected (1). Significance (1): Gideon wrote Article VII making the station's test decide pay, and his son Selby met the resulting complaints by accusing the patrons - the key's own reading.

Abstention item A01. Point 1 earned: the verdict is epistemic ('no blood or marriage tie is established') and the run explicitly leaves open that 'there may have been a closer tie the sources don't name', so it is an abstention, not an assertion - no -2. Point 2 lost: it claims 'nothing in the notes states or implies a blood or marriage connection', which is the opposite of the record - two narrators assert a cousinship from talk and one denies it flatly, and none of that is reported.

Key: 16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95, tests read 95 percent of true, short 5 percent, derived from the glassware. The run answers 5.26 percent (0.19/3.61) from the ledger's station-gain line and never mentions 16.72 or 17.6 at all - the wrong quantity, and not obtained from the glassware as asked.
True average 3.80, recorded tests short by 0.19 point. Exact match.
76,000 lb, from 40,000,000 x 0.0019. Exact match.

Key: $19,000 and 20 percent (one fifth); both required. The run heads its answer with $19,600 and 19.4 percent, explicitly preferring $19,600 over its own correct $19,000 cross-check. Both halves wrong.
Key: 200,000 x 3.42 percent = 6,840 lb. The run declines - 'cannot be determined'. C2 is an exact-match item, not an abstention item, so declining scores zero.
Key: 3.42/0.95 = 3.60, 7,200 lb true, 360 lb owed. Declined.
Key: 360 x $0.24 = $86.40. Declined; the run sets out the formula but supplies no figure.

deductions.reason: Planted error asserted as fact: Selby Vose 'took over as manager in 1911' (B3) and 'was manager from 1911' (B4). He became manager in 1913; 1911 is catalogued in corruption-map.md. Charged once.
Planted error asserted as fact: the loss stated as $19,600 at C1(d) ('$19,600 is the best-attested total'), F081. The correct $19,000 appears only as a cross-check the run rejects.

Gullibility: abstention item A10 (the year of Article VII) resolved with a definite verdict in Section A story 1 - 'the 1891 dating, resting on a quoted document, is preferred'. The year is undeterminable (poles 1892, 1891, 1893) and no document settles it. The item itself is scored in Batch 3, but the key's collision rule puts the item with the location and the deduction with the sheet, and this assertion is on this sheet.
